# Breakout in p5.js

Steve Wozniak built the original in four days; this one is ~90 lines of [p5.js](https://p5js.org) (vendored — no CDN) inside a single HTML cell. The interesting engineering is all collision response:

- **Walls** flip one velocity component — pure reflection.
- **The paddle** is not a wall: where the ball lands sets its outgoing *angle*, which is the entire skill element of the game.
- **Bricks** need to know which face was struck — we compare penetration depths and flip the shallow axis.

The sliders are live: `nb.onChange` feeds the sketch every change, mid-rally. Physics tuning with zero restarts is exactly what the nb bridge is for.

<style>
  body { margin: 0; background: #0f172a; display: flex; justify-content: center; }
</style>
<script src="/shared/lib/p5.js/1.9.4/p5.min.js"></script>
<script>
  var W = 860, H = 580;
  var paddleW = 110, speed = 5;         // live-tuned via nb
  var ball, bricks, lives, score, state; // state: 'serve' | 'play' | 'over' | 'won'

  function resetBricks() {
    bricks = [];
    var colors = ['#f87171', '#fb923c', '#facc15', '#4ade80', '#38bdf8'];
    for (var r = 0; r < 5; r++) {
      for (var c = 0; c < 10; c++) {
        bricks.push({ x: 20 + c * 82, y: 60 + r * 30, w: 74, h: 22,
                      color: colors[r], points: (5 - r) * 10 });
      }
    }
  }

  function serve() {
    ball = { x: W / 2, y: H - 80, vx: 0, vy: 0 };
    state = 'serve';
  }

  function setup() {
    createCanvas(W, H);
    lives = 3; score = 0;
    resetBricks();
    serve();
  }

  function launch() {
    var a = -Math.PI / 2 + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.6;
    ball.vx = Math.cos(a) * speed;
    ball.vy = Math.sin(a) * speed;
    state = 'play';
  }

  function draw() {
    background('#0f172a');
    var px = constrain(mouseX, paddleW / 2, W - paddleW / 2);

    // bricks
    bricks.forEach(function (b) {
      fill(b.color); noStroke(); rect(b.x, b.y, b.w, b.h, 4);
    });
    // paddle
    fill('#e2e8f0'); rect(px - paddleW / 2, H - 30, paddleW, 12, 6);
    // ball
    fill('#f8fafc'); circle(ball.x, ball.y, 14);
    // hud
    fill('#94a3b8'); textSize(14); textAlign(LEFT);
    text('score ' + score + '   lives ' + lives +
         '   paddle ' + paddleW + '   speed ' + speed, 16, 24);

    if (state === 'serve') {
      ball.x = px; ball.y = H - 44;
      fill('#cbd5e1'); textAlign(CENTER); textSize(18);
      text('click to launch', W / 2, H / 2 + 60);
      return;
    }
    if (state === 'over' || state === 'won') {
      fill(state === 'won' ? '#4ade80' : '#f87171');
      textAlign(CENTER); textSize(28);
      text(state === 'won' ? 'CLEARED! click to play again' : 'game over - click to retry',
           W / 2, H / 2 + 60);
      return;
    }

    // keep the current speed setting without changing direction
    var mag = Math.hypot(ball.vx, ball.vy) || 1;
    ball.vx = ball.vx / mag * speed;
    ball.vy = ball.vy / mag * speed;
    ball.x += ball.vx;
    ball.y += ball.vy;

    // walls reflect
    if (ball.x < 7 || ball.x > W - 7) ball.vx *= -1;
    if (ball.y < 7) ball.vy *= -1;

    // paddle sets the angle by WHERE you catch it
    if (ball.vy > 0 && ball.y > H - 37 && ball.y < H - 18 &&
        Math.abs(ball.x - px) < paddleW / 2 + 7) {
      var offset = (ball.x - px) / (paddleW / 2);   // -1 .. 1
      var angle = -Math.PI / 2 + offset * 1.05;      // up to ~60 degrees
      ball.vx = Math.cos(angle) * speed;
      ball.vy = Math.sin(angle) * speed;
    }

    // bricks: flip the axis of shallowest penetration
    for (var i = bricks.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      var b = bricks[i];
      if (ball.x + 7 < b.x || ball.x - 7 > b.x + b.w ||
          ball.y + 7 < b.y || ball.y - 7 > b.y + b.h) continue;
      var overlapX = Math.min(ball.x + 7 - b.x, b.x + b.w - (ball.x - 7));
      var overlapY = Math.min(ball.y + 7 - b.y, b.y + b.h - (ball.y - 7));
      if (overlapX < overlapY) ball.vx *= -1; else ball.vy *= -1;
      score += b.points;
      bricks.splice(i, 1);
      break;
    }
    if (bricks.length === 0) state = 'won';

    // floor
    if (ball.y > H + 10) {
      lives--;
      if (lives <= 0) state = 'over'; else serve();
    }
  }

  function mousePressed() {
    if (state === 'serve') launch();
    else if (state === 'over' || state === 'won') setup();
  }

  function applyState(s) {
    if (typeof s.breakout_paddle === 'number') paddleW = s.breakout_paddle;
    if (typeof s.breakout_speed === 'number') speed = s.breakout_speed;
  }
  nb.onChange(applyState);
  applyState(nb.all());
</script>

## The dissection

- **Serve → play → over** is a tiny state machine; every game you've ever played has one, usually much bigger and usually undocumented.
- The paddle-angle rule (`offset * 1.05`) is the whole game design. Set the multiplier to 0 and the ball reflects like a wall — suddenly you have no aim control and the game is boring. Game feel lives in constants like this.
- The brick collision compares penetration depths — the cheap, robust way to answer "which side did I hit?" without ray casting.

## Try this

- Slide paddle width to 50 and speed to 9 **mid-rally** — the bridge applies it instantly. Find your personal impossible threshold.
- Score multiplier: make the ball speed up 2% per brick (`speed *= 1.02` — note it'll fight the slider's setting; decide who wins, and you've just designed a difficulty system).
- Add a second ball after 20 bricks: push another ball object into an array and loop the physics over it.
- The classic exploit: tunnel up a side channel and let the ball rattle across the top row. Widen the side gap (bricks start at x=20) to make the strategy easier — Woz left that in on purpose.
